title: feat(types)!: refuse both content channels on the E3 residual (nine object views, detail-view, email, password) and repair the shorthand Omit erasure (objectui#9256)
body:
Part of #9256
Clause-②: yes

**Clause-② `yes`, as the claim declared:** twelve published arms stop accepting an authored `children`, and two published TypeScript faces stop erasing the members they inherit. Both narrow an accept set; a contract review is owed before landing.

The E3 residual that the maintainer's ruling on objectui#8284 (comment `5861449497`, Q2 A) moved onto this card: keys with a published arm whose renderer reads **neither** content channel. It also carries the ruling's execution parameter 3, the `InputShorthandSchema` / `UiCalendarSchema` TypeScript `Omit` erasure. objectui#9256 stays open for the rest of family D.

## What changed

- **Narrowed (12 keys):** `object-grid`, `object-form`, `object-kanban`, `object-map`, `object-tree`, `object-view`, `object-gantt`, `object-calendar`, `object-chart`, `detail-view`, `email`, `password`.
  - TypeScript face: `body?: never` and `children?: never`, each with a docblock naming what the node renders instead.
  - zod mirror: `body` and `children` are two `retirementTombstone` members fed ONE string from the new `neitherContentChannelGuidance` builder in `zod/tombstone.zod.ts`. Both stay MEMBERS, so `zod-mirror-parity`'s key sets stay equal.
  - `body` was already refused on these arms (by `BaseSchema`, objectui#6771), except on the `email` / `password` TypeScript face, which the `Omit` erased. It is restated because `BaseSchema`'s refusal names `children` as the remedy, and `children` is dead here too.
- **`Omit` erasure repaired:** `InputShorthandSchema` and `UiCalendarSchema` now inherit through `OmitDeclared` (`form.ts`, not exported). It is a key-remapping mapped type: it drops exactly the named keys and keeps every other named member and the index signature.
  - `ui:calendar` gains no refusal of its own. Its face now re-exposes what `CalendarSchema` declares, so the published TypeScript face refuses `body`, `children` and a `mode` outside the declared enum, which the erased face accepted. Its mirror (a `.extend()` of that one) already refused them.
  - I measured the `ui:calendar` renderer anyway (`renderers/form/calendar.tsx`, typed `CalendarSchema`). It reads `defaultValue`, `mode` and `value`, and no channel.
- **Held (3 keys): `br`, `hr`, `img`.** See "Held, and the question it leaves" below.

## Per-key measurement, taken on `origin/main` `0c50f1863` before any edit

**Instrument.** The TypeScript compiler API, ⛔ not grep. It builds one program per workspace package from that package's own `tsconfig.json`: 40 programs over 1573 source files, on a BUILT tree (turbo build 42/42 first), with `@object-ui/types` resolving to `packages/types/dist`. It files every `.body` / `.children` read (property access, string element access, object destructuring) under the declared type of its receiver.

- 547 channel reads were filed.
- **Lit controls fire:** `ButtonSchema` 1, `DivSchema` 1, `CardSchema` 1, `ContainerSchema` 1 (each `children`).
- **Receiver-reachability control:** the same program sees every narrowed declaration as a receiver of the keys its renderer reads. The zeros below are readings, not blindness.

| key | registration(s) claiming it | registration hop → reader, and the type it reads the node as | `body` / `children` reads under that type | receiver reads (reachability) | arm, TS face: before → after | arm, zod face: before → after | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `object-grid` | `plugin-grid:object-grid` (+ console `registerLazy` of the same plugin) | `ObjectGridRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectGrid` · `ObjectGridSchema` | 0 / 0 | 158 reads, 38 keys | body refused (BaseSchema), children accepted → both refused | same → both refused by name | narrowed |
| `object-form` | `plugin-form:object-form` | `ObjectFormRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectForm` · `ObjectFormSchema` | 0 / 0 | 200 / 44 | same | same | narrowed |
| `object-kanban` | `plugin-kanban:object-kanban` (+ lazy) | `ObjectKanbanRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectKanban` · `ObjectKanbanSchema` | 0 / 0 | 67 / 13 | same | same | narrowed |
| `object-map` | `plugin-map:object-map` (+ lazy) | `ObjectMapRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectMap` · `ObjectMapSchema` | 0 / 0 | 30 / 16 | same | same | narrowed |
| `object-tree` | `plugin-tree:object-tree` (+ lazy) | `ObjectTreeRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectTree` · `ObjectTreeSchema` | 0 / 0 | 13 / 8 | same | same | narrowed |
| `object-view` | `plugin-view:object-view` (and the `view` alias) | `ObjectViewRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectView` · `ObjectViewSchema` | 0 / 0 | 112 / 19 | same | same | narrowed |
| `object-gantt` | `plugin-gantt:object-gantt` (+ lazy) | `ObjectGanttRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectGantt` · `ObjectGanttSchema` | 0 / 0 | 61 / 48 | same | same | narrowed |
| `object-calendar` | `plugin-calendar:object-calendar` (+ lazy) | `ObjectCalendarRenderer` (`any`) → `ObjectCalendar` · `ObjectCalendarSchema` | 0 / 0 | 40 / 12 | same | same | narrowed |
| `object-chart` | `plugin-charts:object-chart` (+ lazy) | `ObjectChartBlock` (`any`) → `ObjectChart` · `ObjectChartSchema` | 0 / 0 | 123 / 15 | same | same | narrowed |
| `detail-view` | `plugin-detail:detail-view` | `DetailViewRenderer` (`any`) → `DetailView` · `DetailViewSchema` | 0 / 0 | 195 / 31 | same | same | narrowed |
| `email` | `ui:email` (`field:email` stands down) | `any` wrapper spreads the node into `InputRenderer` · `InputSchema` | 0 / 0 | 23 / 17 | BOTH accepted (erased `Omit`) → both refused | body refused, children accepted → both refused by name | narrowed |
| `password` | `ui:password` (`field:password` stands down) | same as `email` | 0 / 0 | 23 / 17 | same as `email` | same as `email` | narrowed |
| `br` | `ui:br` | html-elements factory (`any`), void tag: passes `undefined` as the child | reads neither (the one `schema?.children` read is behind the void-tag guard) | n/a (`any`) | body refused, children accepted (family arm) → unchanged | same → unchanged | **held** |
| `hr` | `ui:hr` | same | same | n/a | same | same | **held** |
| `img` | `ui:img` | same | same | n/a | same | same | **held** |

The residual count stays 15: no key reads `children` today. 12 are narrowed and 3 are held.

**`any`-typed receivers, attributed rather than assumed.**

- Every hop above is `any`-typed. Each hop body was read: none contains a channel read.
- The any-typed reads in the eleven hosting files and packages were attributed one by one:
  - React `children` destructured off internal components' own props (`SchemaRenderer` passes no node child as a React child);
  - `document.body` and `err.body`;
  - `TreeNode.children` on the record hierarchy `ObjectTree` builds;
  - `FeedItem.body`;
  - `record:alert`'s own `props.body`, which is another registration.
- The html factory's `schema?.children` read sits behind `isVoid ? undefined : …`.

**Delegation hosts, checked for pass-through.** Every `SchemaRenderer` call in the ten object/detail packages was traced. The node it renders is built one of three ways:

- key by key — `ObjectForm` / `ModalForm` / `DrawerForm` / `TabbedForm` / `SplitForm` / `WizardForm` all build their `form` node that way, and the `form` renderer DOES draw `children`, which is why this was checked;
- from a sub-key — `DetailView`'s `header` / `footer` / tab `content`, `ObjectChart`'s drill-down table;
- or from a generated `object-*` node — `ObjectView` assembles `object-kanban`, `object-calendar`, `object-gallery`, `object-timeline`, `object-gantt`, `object-map`, `object-tree` and `object-chart` from named keys, and every one of those reads neither channel (for gallery and timeline: `packages/plugin-list` and `packages/plugin-timeline` hold no node-channel read).

No host spreads its own node into a node that reads `children`.

**Generic traversers** (`validateChildren` in core, `sdui-parser` `validateTree`, the metadata-admin preview canvases, the vscode validator) walk children to validate or preview. They render nothing and are node-agnostic, as for every row family D already holds.

**objectui#9910 cross-check.** None of the 12 narrowed registrations declares a `children` slot input: a grep over their registration files finds 0 hits, and the lit control is `html-elements.tsx` / `div.tsx`, which do.

**Producers.** `pnpm census:body-dialect --keys` over the 15, plus `ui:calendar` and `input`, with `div` / `card` / `page` / `button` / `p` / `h1` as lit controls in the same pass: 8981 files, 2744 candidate nodes.

- **0** nodes author `children` on any of the 15.
- 1 node authors `body` on `ui:calendar`: it was the family-D TRIPWIRE test line (test bucket), moved by this change.
- The controls read `div` 170 / `card` 183 / `page` 47 `children`.
- Producers derived: none. Nothing was migrated.

## The `Omit` repair — measured on the BUILT d.ts

A probe program under `packages/components` resolved `@object-ui/types` to `packages/types/dist/index.d.ts` (`--traceResolution`). It carried 15 `@ts-expect-error` pins (the 10 object/detail `children`, `email` `children`, `password` `body`, `email` `label: 42`, and the `ui:calendar` `children` and `mode: 'default'`), a lit control (`const n: number = 'x'`), and 12 channel-free controls.

- **On this branch:** exit 0 — every directive used, every control compiles, the lit control fires.
- **On the base dist:** exit 2 with 15 × TS2578, and the lit control is still used.
- The emitted `dist/form.d.ts` declares `OmitDeclared` locally and both heritage clauses use it.

## Red on base, then green — one-shot, the restore proven by state

The predictions were written to a file BEFORE the mutation. The mutation was `git checkout 0c50f1863 -- THE-SEVEN-DECLARATION-FILES`, with every test file at HEAD. It was proven by 7/7 blob hashes equal to BASE plus anchor counts (`neitherContentChannel` 0, `OmitDeclared` 0). The run sat under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths.

| reader | mutated (BASE arms) | restored (HEAD `14fd13c51`) |
|---|---|---|
| vitest, the new pin file | **RED** exit 1 — 73 failed / 90 passed; exactly the predicted 12 × 5 `children` families + 12 `body`-message rows + 1 nested row | **GREEN** 163 / 163 |
| `tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.test.json` | **RED** exit 2 — 18 × TS2578 and 3 × TS2322 (the `Eq` pins) in the new file, plus 3 in `zod-mirror-parity` naming the two re-collapsed pairs and the stale `KnownDrift` row; 0 elsewhere | **GREEN** exit 0 |
| built-d.ts probe (types rebuilt; dist markers 0 → 29 / 6) | **RED** exit 2, 15 × TS2578 | **GREEN** exit 0 |

The restore was proven by 7/7 blob hashes equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty and `git status` clean, both after the restore and at the end.

⚠️ **The `body` rows on the ten object/detail arms are GREEN on base, by design:** `BaseSchema` already refused `body` there. Only their MESSAGE changes, and the message rows are the ones that turn red. `?: never` is erased before vitest runs, so the TypeScript half is read by `tsc` alone. The vitest run cannot see it.

  - `content-channel-family-d-9256.test.ts`: the only edits are forced ones, clear of PR objectui#10714's hunks, which sit in the ListItem and Tabs sections:
    - The file's own `ui:calendar` TRIPWIRE said "when the collapse is repaired this line goes RED … turn it back into a `@ts-expect-error` pair". The repair fired it.
    - The pair moved to the new file. That file lost the tripwire line, its `uiCalendarBody` array entry (32 → 31) and the now-unused `UiCalendarSchema` type import.
    - No pin was added there.
  - `objectql.ts`: the insertion after `ObjectViewSchema`'s last member is clear of PR objectui#10883's `NamedListView` docblock edit.

This branch merged `main` at that commit (merge commit `31bb63bcb`, no rebase, no force-push) and recounted the figures from the merged table; see "Merge round" under Gates.
  - PRs objectui#10888, #10889 and #10892 are textually disjoint, and all three have since merged. `git merge-tree` of the merge head against `main` at `6a7f24e92`, which carries all of them, reports no conflict.
- ⛔ `zod/index.zod.ts` and the `packages/cli` ratchet (objectui#10872) are untouched.

## Collateral that the repair and narrowing made true or false — each measured, none widened

- **`zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`:**
  - The two `Omit` COLLAPSE rows (32 + 26 keys) leave `MirroredUndeclared`. Its figures move from 4 / 60 to 2 / 2, and the class note records the emptying.
  - Restoring the named members NARROWED those faces: a collapsed face accepted every key at `any`. So this is not the "declare the keys" remedy that ledger refuses.
  - The repaired shorthand face now carries `InputSchema`'s `onChange` runtime slot. It enters `KnownDrift` as inherited drift: one entry, one key. After the merge with PR objectui#10890 (which took `ai.zod.ts#AIFormAssistSchema` out, one entry and two keys), the table holds 49 entries / 88 keys, and both header sites say so.
  - The union-arm non-vacuity leg had no multi-arm entry left in this ledger. It now takes the same reader's arm-walking on `KnownDrift` and re-arms here when a multi-arm entry lands.
- **`object-view-spec-parity.test.ts`:** `body` / `children` are redeclared envelope keys on `object-view` now. They are triaged into `SANCTIONED_LOCAL` as refusal-only surface, like `viewTabBar`, and the declared-surface figure moves 24 → 26.
- **`CalendarSchema`'s texts on both faces said the TypeScript `Omit` "collapses … and carries no member".** That became false; they are corrected.
- **Two comments** that spelled the old plain-`Omit` heritage (`index.ts`, `form-barrel-mirror-9406.test.ts`) are corrected.
- **`scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs`** caught my first spelling. It was a computed spread (`...helper(…)`) that the gate cannot resolve, so it stopped judging all eleven arms and its `detail-view` `onTabChange` waiver read stale. The fix, the second commit, declares both members explicitly. Now 49 / 49 reads are judged and 0 are left unjudged.

## Held, and the question it leaves

`br` / `hr` / `img` read neither channel, but their only published arm is `HtmlElementSchema`: ONE object over 38 tags, whose renderer draws `children` for the other 35 (`p`, `h1`, …). Refusing the key on three tags means splitting that family arm, or refining it per tag. Both change a published contract's shape.

- The option the ruling adopted (option A in measurement `5859897857`) reads: "leaving the three void tags to the tier because their arm is the shared HtmlElementSchema family whose per-tag split was ruled out (objectui#9067)".
- The parser tier already names them: the registration declares no `children` slot on a void tag, so `validateTree` reports `not-a-container`.
- A HELD control in the new pin file records the shared-arm fact, so the hold is visible.

That the brief listed them among the keys to narrow is recorded as a conflict in the report, ⛔ not resolved here by guessing.

- **`input` reads neither channel as well.** `InputSchema`: 0 channel reads, 17 keys read; the registration declares no `children` slot.
  - It is this card's remaining family-D name, and it was not in this claim.
  - Its old hold-out ground ("a TS `Omit` carries nothing") is gone with this repair: a tombstone on `InputSchema` now propagates on both faces.
  - Carrier: the next objectui#9256 slice.
- **`PartialSchema`'s docblock in `index.ts`** says every generic re-spelling of its `Omit` collapses for the same `keyof T` reason. `OmitDeclared` is a generic spelling that does not: this PR measures it on two faces.
  - Carrier: the next objectui#9256 slice, which touches the same `Omit` subject. objectui#6397, that alias's card, is closed.

  - Carrier: the next objectui#9256 slice.
